key_insight: An imposed magnetic field increases traveling-roll dynamics in 2D Rayleigh–Bénard convection and promotes intermittent roll splitting/breaking, helping drive the system toward chaotic and turbulent behavior.
engineering_relevance: This suggests magnetic control can be used to alter convection topology and stability in magnetohydrodynamic heat-transfer systems, with implications for flow control and turbulence management.
method: Baseline 2D Rayleigh–Bénard convection was simulated without a magnetic field across a range of reduced Rayleigh numbers.
A background magnetic field was then introduced and the transition from traveling rolls to chaotic dynamics was examined.
Velocity-field topology was analyzed to identify saddle-center collisions and magnetic reconnection events.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations showing that, with increasing reduced Rayleigh number and under magnetic forcing, the flow transitions from traveling rolls to chaotic traveling rolls after an attractor-merging crisis, with intermittent magnetic reconnection and roll splitting.
watch_item: The findings are based on 2D simulations, so extension to fully 3D convection and quantitatively different parameter regimes may be limited.
paper_title: Transition to chaos in two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection: the role of the magnetic field
